P1 · 24 nearly-identical cards stacked vertically. No grouping by value tier, deadline, category, or owner. No filtering, no sort. A CPO scanning this sees "wall of work" and bounces.
P2 · Each card opens "Open decision" — the CTA implies a binary; but most cards lead to a multi-week sourcing event. CTA promises more than it can deliver in one click.
P2 · No "what's overdue" / "what's blocked" visual hierarchy. Every card is equally weighted.

Works well · 11-stage rail gives clear lifecycle orientation. Locked stages (greyed) signal what's gated. The two-pane workspace pattern is a reasonable mental model.
P1 · Sentinel chat panel takes ~40% width on EVERY stage. Strategy work and Executive Decision need different proportions — drafting wants chat, deciding wants document focus.
P1 · Artifact codes (d01_strategy_memo, d05_scope_memo) visible in tile labels. The L6 audit caught this; humanization PR didn't cover this surface.
P1 · Header "6 DB-backed documents" + the "source_artifacts" tag visible — internal-product language in CXO-facing view.
P2 · The actual stage work (Strategy Memo, Pricing Workbook, etc.) sits BELOW the artifact shelf. Below the fold. The shelf shows the same 6 docs on every stage; only the bottom changes.
P2 · No page-1 executive summary. On Executive Decision stage you should land on the recommendation, not the artifact shelf.
P2 · Two AI disclaimers stack permanently in the chat panel ("HUMAN APPROVAL REQUIRED" + "AI may produce errors"). After 50 views they're wallpaper.

14 · Cross-cutting patterns observed

PATTERN 1 · The bones are right; execution is loud

Every page has the right concept (lifecycle rail, artifact shelf, agent rail, value metrics, evidence ledger). But each element is rendered at full strength with no hierarchy. Apple-style would dim 3 of 4 so the eye knows where to look.

PATTERN 2 · Sentinel chat is undifferentiated by stage

~40% of every event canvas is the chat panel. Strategy stage needs chat (drafting). Executive Decision stage needs document focus (deciding). Same UI footprint, different mental task.

PATTERN 3 · Internal taxonomy leaks across surfaces

d01_strategy_memo · "DB-backed documents" · "STEWARD NEEDS" · "Deterministic event report" · "source_artifacts" tag · [Scaffold] badges · "Substrate signal: 0 vendor_contracts rows on file." PR #2868 humanized labels on artifact tiles but didn't sweep deal-pack, CXO report, intake form, or event-canvas chrome.

PATTERN 4 · Lead with the workings, not the answer

Executive Decision stage opens to the artifact shelf. Deal Pack opens to Demand Challenge (Stage 0). CXO Report opens to a cover slide. None of them lead with: "Northstar selected. $13.21M TCO. Trade-off: gave up incumbent stability, gained 3-yr benchmark right. Two dissents tracked. Approved by Carlos Rivera on 2026-06-04."

PATTERN 5 · Lifecycle stops at Selection in deliverables

Stages 10 (Transition) and 11 (Value) exist in the event canvas rail and at /value, but they're absent from the Deal Pack and largely absent from the CXO Report. The Board's most important question — "did we save what you promised?" — has no surface that answers it well.

PATTERN 6 · /source/events is qualitatively better than every other page

The portfolio view reads like a Stripe dashboard. The decision queue reads like a wall of work. The event canvas reads like an internal admin tool. The contrast tells us the team knows how to design at executive grade — they just haven't applied that lens to every surface yet.

PATTERN 7 · Disclaimers and safety language compound to wallpaper

"HUMAN APPROVAL REQUIRED" + "AI may produce errors" + "CITATION GAP" + "Awaiting authoring" + "Self-approval notice" — each correct in isolation; stacked, they're chrome that the user learns to ignore. Trust is built by withholding most banners until they actually fire on a specific risk.
